source_row.rationale: Primary adrenal insufficiency can produce fatigue or weakness, hypotension from volume depletion, salt craving from mineralocorticoid deficiency, and hyperpigmentation associated with elevated ACTH, so Option B is correct. Cushing syndrome reflects glucocorticoid excess, acromegaly reflects growth-hormone excess, and primary hyperaldosteronism typically produces hypertension rather than this pattern.
source_row.source_detail: Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Primary Adrenal Insufficiency, clinical features and diagnostic considerations: glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid deficiency can cause fatigue or weakness, volume depletion and hypotension, salt craving, and hyperpigmentation from elevated ACTH in primary disease. Endocrine Society Primary Adrenal Insufficiency guideline remains the current society guideline resource; live source and current status rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, endocrine/vascular emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

source_row.stem: A client has fatigue, hypotension, salt craving, and patchy hyperpigmentation. Which endocrine disorder best fits this pattern?
